SOAH DOCKET NO. 473-26-16349
PUC DOCKET NO. 59475
JEANETTE VRABEL MIKSCH’S  INITIAL brief
Intervenor Jeanette Vrabel Miksch, pro se intervenor, files this Initial Brief in the docket mentioned above. 
The hearing of the Merits did not provide me and others to have an opportunity to be heard due to the overwhelming number of intervenors who had witnesses.  I would like to express that the PUC and Applicants lack in providing guidance on the procedural process and deadlines. For the landowners who do not have devices such as a computer and smartphone they could not/would not have received the short notice information except by a family member or neighbor since it was all posted on the PUC Interchange and that was the only way to communicate with the parties. I hope for future cases, this is taken into consideration.

  
In summary, Links B3, D2, E3 affects my property, and I am opposed to the 765KV transmission line project however specifically oppose any route that uses Link B3, D2, E3 for the reasons set forth below.

I have filed written testimony (Item 4133) that was admitted into evidence regarding how Links B3, D2, E3 would affect my property, as well as other landowners did, that are affected by these same links. These same links affect other family members’ properties, which are close in proximity. 

The proposed E3 link would cut into my property and D2 link would bisect into E3 which would be on my property or on my father’s property that borders my property. 

These proposed links would affect and place a permanent burden on my livelihood, agricultural operations, cattle, wildlife, family life and rural community and these make for strong evidence of the opposition to the 765Kv transmission line project, but specifically links B3, D2, E3.
But there are more substantive reasons that the 765Kv transmission line should not be built. 
The proposed routes including links B3, D2, E3 would affect agriculture land utilized to raise crops and cattle to contribute to the food supply.  The agriculture land is gradually becoming less and less due to the influx of growth of housing and businesses.  In addition, this proposed alternative route for a 765Kv transmission line would consume even more agriculture land. Again diminishing the amount of agriculture land even more. 
The agricultural equipment used is computerized and includes GPS therefore, in my opinion, the 765Kv line may affect farming operations and operational hazards for those who must work around it on a daily basis. This 765Kv transmission line may not only impact productivity of the farmers but may also affect productivity of the crop yields.
The electric fence line around the pasture areas, for retaining cattle, may also be affected by the 765Kv transmission line voltage.
 
I respectfully ask that the ALJs would thoughtfully look into other alternatives of how power can be provided in the needed area, without building the massive 765Kv transmission line.  If the 765Kv transmission line should be approved, then I would also request that there be a requirement as part of the approval that landowners be compensated by the utility companies for use of landowner’s land over the life of the transmission line being on their property. Example would be a quarterly or monthly payment.

In conclusion, for the reasons stated above, I oppose the whole 765Kv transmission line project but specifically oppose links B3, D2, and E3. 
Respectfully submitted,

/s/Jeanette Vrabel Miksch
